pep.label: Census PEP
pep.notes: Fresh population/housing replacement with strong 2024 coverage; recent-history only.

laus.label: BLS LAUS
laus.notes: Fresh labor signal with recent-history window; useful despite shorter history.

bea.label: BEA Income
bea.notes: Best new structural income/wealth family; broad history and strong coverage.

lodes.label: LEHD / LODES
lodes.notes: Good labor/mobility structure but only 2020-2023 native history and higher missingness.

noaa_climate.label: NOAA Climate
noaa_climate.notes: Historical county climate panel with strong latest-year coverage.

storm.label: NOAA Storm Events
storm.notes: Historical disruption/damage context; useful risk-side complement to climate normals.

epa_sld.label: EPA Smart Location
epa_sld.notes: High-value structural signal bundle, but current build uses a static 2021-vintage layer across all years.

cdc_places.label: CDC PLACES
cdc_places.notes: Current release snapshot only; keep out of historical training for now.

nces.label: NCES Structure + Finance
nces.notes: FY23/2022-23 snapshot enrichment only; keep out of historical training for now.

nfip.label: OpenFEMA NFIP
nfip.notes: Latest snapshot, not a point-in-time historical panel.

fcc_broadband.label: FCC Broadband
fcc_broadband.notes: Landed as a first-pass county broadband snapshot; useful context, but still snapshot-style and missing provider competition.

fbi_ucr.label: FBI UCR / CDE
fbi_ucr.notes: Landed as a conservative county safety layer, but coverage semantics and packed-layout caution keep it out of historical training for now.

core_findings: Current horizon feature artifacts predate the newer Wave 2 landings, so overlap with newly added source families is still effectively zero until feature reselection is rerun.
The strongest historical-safe additions for the next retrain pass are BEA income, Census PEP, BLS LAUS, NOAA climate, NOAA storm events, and LEHD/LODES.
CDC PLACES, NCES, and NFIP should stay panel-only until a point-in-time vintage strategy is defined.
EPA Smart Location is valuable, but it should be explicitly reviewed before the next retrain because the current layer is static and 2021-vintage rather than truly historical.

FCC broadband and FBI UCR are now landed as panel-only enrichments rather than true deferred sources, but both should stay out of historical training until their time semantics and aggregation confidence improve.

rationale: The heavier NHDPlus lane is operationally real on both island and mainland/coastal proofs.
State-level semantics are useful, especially coastline/estuary/flowline fields, but core proxy-vs-upgrade deltas remain large enough to require more geography before promotion.
The combined HI+NJ downstream product movement is small, so the lane is safe to keep testing as a sidecar without replacing the live hydro proxy.

next_experiments: Use the completed specialist comparison as a baseline, then test one 3yr target/model treatment at a time without replacing live artifacts.

recommendation.decision: Keep this as a useful treatment read, but do not promote unless it improves both temporal health and live ranking interaction versus the current stack.
Post-GFC plus label winsorization is the strongest primary-model treatment so far, but no candidate beats the existing specialist on MAE or gives enough live top-25 alignment to justify promotion.
Blending can improve primary-model error, but the best low-error blends still do not beat the standalone specialist on MAE or provide strong enough live final-top-25 alignment for promotion.

Stable top-10 feature restriction materially improves temporal R2/MAE, but it weakens top-k ranking quality and live final-top-25 alignment. Treat it as a promising variance-control ingredient, not a standalone promotion.

This is the strongest 3yr candidate so far on combined temporal fit and live alignment. It should advance to a full scoring-stack gate, but should not be promoted directly from this local artifact-only experiment because NDCG@25 is still below the best ranking-only signals and the live final-top-25 overlap is only partial.
